title: One habitat-label swap can reverse each bird drought abundance contrast in three samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested habitat specialist-minus-other drought abundance responses within three bird study samples from a 2024 public release. Equal species means gave contrasts of +0.017, -0.883 and -0.053 standardized units. Each sign can reverse when one specialist and one other species exchange labels. Both negative contrasts survived each single species omission. All three simultaneous normal-reference intervals include zero when sampling correlations can take any valid value. The test uses 137 rows and 109 study-species units in Australia and Hawaii. It does not establish a common specialist deficit. Broad habitat labels, detection, selected studies, uncertain covariance and incomplete event dates limit inference. The extract does not support a balanced independent-period test. No air pollution effect is tested. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and source hashes are included. Raw source data stay external.

display.caption: Within-study habitat contrasts, simultaneous normal-reference intervals under arbitrary sampling covariance, and all one-pair habitat-label swaps. Swap ranges are sensitivity ranges, not confidence intervals.
